title: Welcome to the feature tour
text: Welcome to the feature tour of Keeping Crafts Alive. This microsite helps school pupils, college and university students, career changers and parents discover heritage craft careers, apprenticeships and virtual work experience across the U K. It covers forty-two crafts in seven domains, from built heritage to boats and wheels. First, a few quick stops on this home page, and then the guide continues page by page.

title: Four simple menus
text: Everything sits under four headings: Explore crafts, Try a V W E, Plan my future, and For teachers and partners. The same headings appear on every page, so visitors always know where they are.

title: The heritage sector, together
text: Historic England, the National Trust, English Heritage, the Church of England, Heritage Crafts, the livery companies and training partners each take a role. This shows who does what, so the whole sector can see its part in keeping crafts alive.

title: A route for every learner
text: Choose school pupil, college student, university student, career changer or parent. You get a step-by-step route, and you can tick steps off as you go, so every visitor has a clear next step.

title: Craft finder
text: Four quick questions match each learner to the craft domains that suit them. It turns, I don't know what I want to do, into a short list of ideas in a couple of minutes.

title: Explore 42 crafts
text: Seven domains, with six crafts in each. Every craft shows its Red List status, its link to science, and how it aligns with key stage five.

title: Private partner dashboards
text: Reach, inclusion and progression data are for funders and partners only, behind a sign-in. The public site never shows them.

title: Continue the tour on each page
text: From here the guide moves page by page, twelve stops in all. Start with the V W E library, or jump to any stop you like.

title: VWE library
text: The V W E library has forty-two craft spotlights across seven domains, each with a thirty-minute key stage three taster, and a five-day placement for key stage four and five. Filter by domain, stage or Red List status, switch on available now to see the Built Heritage pilot, and ask to be told when a craft launches.

title: A day on site
text: Here's a day on site as a Heritage Stonemason, arriving at the church tower. Work through the steps on the left, try the myth-busting quiz and the spot-the-decay drill, and write your site diary to get A I feedback.

title: One post, five days
text: This shows how a V W E works, using one post across five days. Pick a day to see its spotlight role, its science link and its skill drill. Compare the live construction V W E with the heritage version, and see the evidence report that learners apply with.

title: Careers planner
text: The careers planner gives each learner a step-by-step plan. Choose a target craft and your stage, and the plan lays out the next steps in order. Tick them off as you go.

title: How you can progress
text: Every domain has a career ladder. Pick a domain to see its ladder, and click a rung for the training and next moves. It shows how far a first role in a craft can lead.

title: Colleges, courses and bursaries
text: This page connects learners to training. Choose a domain and your stage, see the matching apprenticeship standards and T Levels, and browse specialist fellowships and bursaries.

title: Partners and opportunities
text: Pick a partner role to see who is involved, open a domain hub, and filter opportunities by type and nation. It shows learners where the real openings are.

title: Linked lessons
text: Science lessons linked to V W Es. Filter by domain and key stage, and see which crafts each lesson leads into. Every teacher gets a way into heritage careers through their own subject.

title: Teacher training
text: Teacher training is organised by craft domain. Pick a domain, work through the four short modules, and claim your C P D certificate.

title: Lesson unit library
text: The unit library puts lessons in teaching order. Pick a unit to see its lessons in sequence. Each unit ends in a taster or a V W E, so the science comes first, then the work experience.

title: School sign-up
text: Finally, school sign-up. Work through four steps, and see how learning data is kept safe. That's the tour. Thank you for watching.
